evidence.quote: Valar Atomics announced a partnership with Nvidia to explore AI data centers powered directly by advanced nuclear energy, marking a first for the industry.
evidence.one_line: Valar Atomics announced a partnership with Nvidia to explore AI data centers powered by advanced nuclear energy (announced Wednesday, 2026-07-01).
evidence.speaker: Valar Atomics

evidence.quote: The companies are considering a 30-megawatt, nearly waterless data center in Utah using Valar’s Ward250 reactor and Nvidia’s water-efficient cooling technology.
evidence.one_line: Companies are considering a 30 MW, nearly waterless data center in Utah using the Ward250 reactor and Nvidia cooling technology.
evidence.speaker: Deseret News (reporter)

evidence.quote: Valar Atomics and Nvidia are exploring the deployment of a 30 megawatt data center, fully powered by their nuclear reactor.
evidence.one_line: Valar and Nvidia are exploring a 30 MW data center fully powered by the Valar reactor.
evidence.speaker: Deseret News (reporter)

evidence.quote: The Ward250’s helium cooling system, combined with Nvidia’s new technology, will allow the data center to operate with almost no water use. The proposed size is 300 times smaller than the approved Stratos data center in Box Elder County.
evidence.one_line: Proposed 30 MW data center is about 300 times smaller than the approved Stratos data center in Box Elder County.
evidence.speaker: Deseret News (reporter)

evidence.quote: Nvidia recently announced its new AI factory design, DSX, which uses a highly water-efficient direct liquid cooling system. Water pumped through the factory remains at 113°F to eliminate the need for power-hungry water chillers.
evidence.one_line: Nvidia recently announced its DSX AI factory design using direct liquid cooling with water at 113°F, eliminating water chillers.
evidence.speaker: Deseret News (reporter)

evidence.quote: Their reactor, the Ward250, went critical on June 18, and it is now generating 100 kilowatts of electricity.
evidence.one_line: Valar's Ward250 reactor went critical on June 18 and is now generating 100 kW of electricity.
evidence.speaker: Deseret News (reporter)

evidence.quote: Before Valar Atomics can generate power commercially, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission will need to license their reactor. In a recent editorial board meeting with the Deseret News, NRC chairman Ho Nieh said the commission is hoping to shorten federal licensing review times to less than 18 months.
evidence.one_line: NRC chairman Ho Nieh said the commission hopes to shorten federal licensing review times to less than 18 months.
evidence.speaker: Ho Nieh

candidates.question: Will Nvidia and Valar Atomics sign a binding agreement to build the 30 MW nuclear-powered data center in Utah by 2027-01-31?

rungs.label: Yes
rungs.condition: A signed binding agreement for the 30 MW Utah data center is public by 2027-01-31

rungs.label: No
rungs.condition: No such signed binding agreement is public by 2027-01-31
